## [PDF page 14]
Division 6 – Counting of Votes in the  
Office of the Chief Electoral Officer
Counting procedures at Election’s Canada administrative  
centre in Ottawa
This section covers special ballots from Canadian electors living abroad, electors living  
in Canada but away from their electoral district, Canadian Armed Forces members who  
voted at a military poll and incarcerated electors.
Verification process
Before the count of special ballots returned to Office of the Chief Electoral Officer  
(OCEO) can begin, the outer envelope of each special ballot voting kit is examined by a  
pair of special ballot officers (SBOs), who compare the information on the envelope with  
the information on the elector’s application.
If the SBOs determine that any of the exclusion criteria set out in sections 267(1) or (2)  
of the Canada Elections Act have been met, the envelope is set aside unopened and  
the reason is recorded on a label. These labels are then signed by the two SBOs and  
the Special Voting Rules Administrator.
All the remaining sealed outer envelopes are then sorted by electoral district and sent to  
preparation for the count.
Counting process
Given the large number of special ballots counted at the OCEO (over 325,000 in the  
45th general election and nearly 186,000 and 262,000 in the 44th and in the  
43rd general elections, respectively), this count must begin before election day.
SBOs—who are appointed by the Chief Electoral Officer (CEO) on the recommendation  
of political parties according to a ratio set out in the Act—count the ballots. If political  
parties do not recommend enough SBOs, the CEO appoints them.
Counting begins on a date the CEO sets or, if no earlier date is set, five days before  
election day. During the 45th general election, counting started on the 10th day before  
election day (Friday, April 18, 2025) and finished the day after election day (Tuesday,  
April 29, 2025). Once the count was finished, the results for each of the 343 electoral  
districts were sent to the returning officers to be added to the overall voting results in  
their respective district.

centre at 440 Coventry Road in Ottawa so they could observe the counting process for  
the 45th general election. Political parties were notified of the count days via the  
Political Entities Service Centre.
Setting aside of outer envelopes

  The information on the outer envelope does not correspond to the information on the  
elector’s Application for Registration and Special Ballot.  
  The declaration on the outer envelope was not signed by the elector (or the person  
assisting the elector).  
  The elector’s correct electoral district cannot be ascertained.  
  The outer envelope was received after election day, 6 p.m., Eastern time.  
  The elector has voted more than once.

We might need to find the "Special Ballot Report" for each election, like 2021 44th general election, 2019 43rd, 2015 42nd, 2011 41st, 2008 40th. We need the province-level numbers of valid votes (by special voting rules). Then sum.

Alternatively, Elections Canada might provide aggregated totals in the reports, or separate provincial reports. Search for "Special Ballot Report 40th general election Quebec valid votes".
